name: Larsen & Toubro Ltd
title: Larsen & Toubro Ltd - 500510 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record order book of ₹7.40 lakh crore (+28%) and 22% inflow growth, but FY26 margin pressure from execution issues in Infrastructure and Energy, with the Group PBDIT margin slipping to 10.2% from 10.3%.

triggers.label: Margin pressure from execution issues
triggers.quote: Overall margin performance was impacted by execution-related time and cost pressures in the Infrastructure and Energy segments

triggers.label: Order book ₹7.40 lakh crore, +28%
triggers.quote: Your Company's Order Book stood at a record high of ₹ 7.40 lakh crore, registering a growth of 28% year-on-year.

red_flags.label: Execution-related cost pressures and higher provisioning
red_flags.quote: including higher provisioning on contract assets and customer receivables

summary.headline: L&T FY26 record order inflow of ₹4.36 lakh crore (+22%) and order book of ₹7.40 lakh crore (+28%); recurring PAT ₹17,238 crore (+18%).
summary.overview: This document is the FY26 Integrated Annual Report / shareholder letter and MD&A for Larsen & Toubro, not a Q2 FY27 earnings call transcript, so it covers the full year to March 31, 2026 rather than the quarter. Group revenue rose 11.8% to ₹2,85,874 crore and consolidated PAT rose 7% to ₹16,084 crore, with recurring PAT up 18%. Standalone PAT fell 42% to ₹6,287 crore on a one-time gratuity charge from the New Labour Codes and an LTMRHL impairment, while standalone recurring PAT rose 26%. Management flagged margin pressure from execution issues in Infrastructure and Energy, and is divesting non-core assets (Nabha Power, L&T Metro Hyderabad) while launching Lakshya 2031.

segments.name: Infrastructure Projects
segments.commentary: Order inflow ₹1,99,064 crore (+14.9%); revenue ₹1,35,345 crore (+3.1%); operating margin 6.9% vs 6.4%. Water & Effluent Treatment revenue hit by Jal Jeevan Mission funding pauses.

segments.name: Energy Projects
segments.commentary: Order inflow ₹1,36,921 crore (+56.4%); revenue ₹54,889 crore (+34.9%); operating margin fell to 6.8% from 8.5% on legacy Hydrocarbon job cost pressure.

segments.name: Hi-Tech Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Order inflow ₹8,366 crore (-54.2%, high base); revenue ₹14,489 crore (+42.3%); margin 16.7% vs 17.3%.

segments.name: IT & Technology Services
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹53,497 crore (+11.3%), 91% international; operating margin steady at 19.5%. LTM and LTTS account for most of the revenue.

segments.name: Financial Services (L&T Finance)
segments.commentary: Retail book above ₹1,19,500 crore, 98% retailised, rated AAA domestic; gold loan business of Paul Merchants acquired with 130 branches.

guidance_outlook: Lakshya 2031 (FY27–FY31) five-year plan targets continued EPC and manufacturing momentum with improved profitability, and a 2x improvement in workforce productivity.
Management expects Energy and offshore demand to remain sustained, though West Asia conflict may cause near-term headwinds for some businesses.
Final dividend of ₹38 per share recommended for FY26.
Nabha Power divestment to Torrent Power (EV ₹6,889 crore) expected to complete in Q1 FY27; L&T Metro Hyderabad sale (₹1,461.47 crore) expected by June 30, 2026.
Group targets water neutrality by 2035 and carbon neutrality by 2040.
capex_capacity: Group capex (net) ₹4,469 crore in FY26 vs ₹3,541 crore in FY25; standalone capex ₹1,915 crore.
Larsen & Toubro Vyoma operational capacity 26 MW (Chennai, Panvel); 36 MW AI-ready data centre under development at Mahape, scalable to 100 MW over three years.
10 KTPA green hydrogen plant under construction at Panipat, Haryana; 300 KTPA green ammonia JDA with ITOCHU at Kandla.
Kattupalli Upgradation Project being converted into a specialised offshore wind hub; new EPS campus in Coimbatore (40 acres).
Renewables portfolio: 38 GWp solar PV, 15 GWh BESS, 1.8 GW wind.
demand_pricing: International orders 52% of order book; standalone international share of order book 43%; Group revenue 54% international.
Private sector share of the order book rose to 39% from 28%.
Management is pursuing a selective, disciplined bidding approach with sector and geography guardrails; competitive intensity is high in government tenders.
Hydrocarbon in India faces cost pressure in legacy jobs; West Asia tender timing expected broadly unchanged per client interactions.
Working capital improved: Group net working capital at 4.1% of sales vs 11.0%; customer advances rose on new awards.

qa_highlights.question: No Q&A session is present in this document; it is the FY26 Integrated Annual Report, not a Q2 FY27 earnings call transcript.
qa_highlights.answer: Not applicable. The document contains no analyst questions or management answers, so this section is empty.

risks_watch: West Asia (GCC is about one-third of revenue; around 100 project sites) conflict affecting vendors, shipping, insurance and project timelines.
Margin pressure from execution issues in Infrastructure and Energy, including higher provisioning on contract assets and receivables; MCO costs rose to 67.5% of revenue.
Jal Jeevan Mission funding pause and customer funding constraints in Water business.
Gratuity one-time charge from New Labour Codes; further labour cost increases from implementation.
Rupee weakness (about ₹93-94/USD in March 2026) and commodity price volatility, with hedging covering most aluminium and copper exposure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order momentum and balance sheet, with cautious language on West Asia and execution margins. Management says the region impact has been limited so far, but near-term uncertainty remains.
key_quotes: The conflict in the region has barely impacted us. It is business as usual at the 100 odd project sites there, with no material disruption to invoicing or collections.
Group Order Inflows for the year stood at a record high of ₹ 4.36 lakh crore, up 22% year-on-year, driven by order wins in Infrastructure and Energy sectors.

growth.why: The brief is the FY26 annual report, not the Q2 FY27 call, so no quarter-specific or FY27 numeric revenue guidance is given; the record order book of ₹7.40 lakh crore (+28%) and capacity additions such as the 26 MW data centre and 36 MW Mahape build provide partial backing for growth, with Lakshya 2031 targets not quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Group EBITDA margin slipped to 10.2% from 10.3% in FY26, Energy operating margin fell to 6.8% from 8.5% on legacy Hydrocarbon job cost pressure, and MCO costs rose to 67.5% of revenue.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 26 MW Vyoma data centre is already operational, and the 36 MW Mahape AI data centre and 10 KTPA Panipat green hydrogen plant are under construction, but no commissioning dates are given and the sizes are small against group scale.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book reached ₹7,40,327 crore (+27.8% YoY) and order inflow ₹4,35,590 crore (+22.1%), supporting execution volumes, though FY26 revenue grew only 11.8% and Infrastructure revenue just 3.1%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Group net capex rose to ₹4,469 crore in FY26 from ₹3,541 crore, and Lakshya 2031 and the offshore wind hub at Kattupalli are planned, but the brief does not quantify utilisation or new capex amounts.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance numbers were given, and management flagged execution-driven margin pressure in Infrastructure and Energy plus West Asia uncertainty.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: West Asia conflict may hit vendors, shipping and timelines across GCC projects (about one-third of revenue), and Jal Jeevan Mission funding pauses are hitting the Water business.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Lakshya 2031 five-year plan starts FY27 with targets not quantified, and the 36 MW AI data centre is scalable to 100 MW over three years.

rows.label: Nabha Power and L&T Metro Hyderabad divestments
rows.why: Nabha Power sale to Torrent Power (EV ₹6,889 crore) expected to complete in Q1 FY27 and the Metro Hyderabad sale (₹1,461.47 crore) by June 30, 2026, so both are on a firm timetable.

rows.label: Private sector and international order mix shift
rows.why: Private share of order book rose to 39% from 28%, and international orders are 52% of the ₹7.40 lakh crore book, which supports revenue visibility.

rows.label: Working capital release
rows.why: Group net working capital fell to 4.1% of sales from 11.0%, with customer advances rising on new awards, and net debt:equity improved to 0.35:1 from 0.60:1.

tone.note: Management was confident on order momentum, the balance sheet and working capital, and cautious on West Asia exposure and execution margins in Infrastructure and Energy. The brief is the FY26 annual report with no Q&A, so analyst tone could not be assessed.
